output.title: Decreasing Students' Stress Through Time Management Training

scenes.narration: Mental health among university students causes concern worldwide, with Pierceall and Keim reporting that seventy-five percent of community college students perceive moderate stress.
scenes.layout_description: A central hand-drawn globe sits beside a student at a desk, accented with a yellow stress indicator.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist black ink line drawing on cream background showing a student hunched over books next to a globe, highlighted by an orange circular stress glow.

scenes.narration: Heightened perceived stress is linked to student underachievement, course dropout, and depression, while some students report using alcohol or smoking for coping.
scenes.layout_description: Three vertical sketch panels illustrate academic struggle, leaving university, and unhealthy coping habits with yellow accents.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink sketch displaying a downward arrow across an open textbook, an exit door outline, and warning symbols highlighted in orange ink.

scenes.narration: Studies indicate that time demands, such as high workload, time pressure, and self-organized learning, represent serious problems linked to higher undergraduate student stress levels.
scenes.layout_description: A ticking clock towers over a large stack of course materials drawn with simple black line art.
scenes.visual_prompt: Line drawing of a large analog clock face with an orange accent hand looming over towering piles of folders and binders.

scenes.narration: Surveying more than one thousand undergraduate students, Van der Meer and colleagues described managing study time as a considerable concern for many learners.
scenes.layout_description: A crowd outline surrounds a large notepad inscribed with time management notes in hand-drawn lettering.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple black ink outlines of many student silhouettes encircling an open notebook with a yellow bookmark ribbon.

scenes.narration: Although universities are urged to offer support programs, Adamson and colleagues noted that evidence-based time management interventions for students still remain very scarce.
scenes.layout_description: An empty library shelf holds only a single marked folder, highlighted in bright yellow ink.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink drawing of a wide university hall with mostly empty bookshelves and a single notebook glowing with an orange outline.

scenes.narration: Prior research by Häfner and colleagues found a preventive effect, but no intervention study had yet demonstrated a decrease in students' perceived stress.
scenes.layout_description: A split comparison diagram shows a flat stress line contrasted with an unproven downward slope.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line graph showing a flat horizontal black line next to a dotted descending line circled in yellow ink.

scenes.narration: This study evaluated whether time management training reduces perceived stress, fosters perceived control of time, and maintains stable effects across four full weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A central question mark connects three cleanly drawn sketch cards representing stress, time control, and a four-week calendar.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink illustration of a question mark in orange ink pointing toward a downward arrow, an open stopwatch, and a small calendar block.

scenes.narration: Theoretically, time management involves assessing time, setting goals, planning, and monitoring activities, which is assumed to enhance perceived control of time and reduce stress.
scenes.layout_description: A horizontal four-step cycle flows across the slide with small sketch icons and yellow arrows.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist diagram with four ink nodes showing an hourglass, a bullseye target, a daily checklist, and a magnifying glass.

scenes.narration: Past student studies yielded mixed results; some found correlations with anxiety, whereas Macan and others reported non-significant links with somatic or job-induced tension.
scenes.layout_description: A balanced scale holds conflicting research icons rendered in black line art.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple hand-drawn scale with one pan holding an anxiety symbol and the other holding a question mark circled in orange.

scenes.narration: The authors hypothesized that the training would increase perceived control of time, reduce perceived stress, while self-reported external demands would remain completely unchanged.
scenes.layout_description: Three clean summary boxes display directional arrows for time control, perceived stress, and unchanged external demands.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three sketched panels showing an upward green-tinted ink arrow, a downward orange arrow, and a horizontal flat yellow bar.

scenes.narration: To test this idea, the researchers selected a non-equivalent dependent variable design, also called an internal referencing strategy, examining one single student training cohort.
scenes.layout_description: A single group of participants is drawn branching out to multiple measurement channels on cream paper.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink sketch of a group of student icons funneling into parallel measurement tracks highlighted with soft yellow lines.

scenes.narration: As Frese and colleagues argued, this evaluation design does not require a pseudotraining group because it rules out Hawthorne, placebo, and testing effects.
scenes.layout_description: A quote box outline encloses protective shields blocking out testing and placebo biases.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn quotation marks enclosing a drawn shield deflecting dashed ink arrows labeled with testing and Hawthorne effects.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress was measured using the tension scale, alongside perceived control of time, whereas the external demands scale served as an uninfluenced control variable.
scenes.layout_description: A clipboard displays three labeled measurement meters drawn in ink with orange accents.
scenes.visual_prompt: Drawing of a wooden clipboard holding a survey form with three rating scales, the bottom scale highlighted by an orange frame.

scenes.narration: The homogeneous intervention lasted four hours, focusing theoretically on prioritizing, establishing proximal goals, developing strategies, daily planning with implementation intentions, and progress monitoring.
scenes.layout_description: A four-hour clock icon sits above five connected process cards on a cream background.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink line art of a clock marked at four hours, leading to sketches of task prioritization and calendar scheduling.

scenes.narration: Participants reflected on study activities, set challenging goals with deadlines, planned realistic daily study schedules to avoid distractions, and checked completed tasks daily.
scenes.layout_description: A student desk view displays an open daily planner, a focused study lamp, and completed checkmarks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Overhead minimalist line drawing of a study desk with an organized daily schedule and small yellow checkmarks beside tasks.

scenes.narration: The researchers recruited forty-eight undergraduate students across various faculties at a German university, offering no external incentives for taking part in the training.
scenes.layout_description: A university building sketch is flanked by forty-eight small student tally icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple ink sketch of a university pediment banner with a group of diverse student avatars gathered below.

scenes.narration: All participants completed pretest measures; twenty-seven returned questionnaires two weeks after training, and twenty-three returned questionnaires four weeks later before final semester exams began.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline flows across three checkpoints showing the exact participant retention numbers.
scenes.visual_prompt: A horizontal black ink timeline with three numbered stops marked 48, 27, and 23 inside yellow circles.

scenes.narration: The final twenty-three participants averaged 23.30 years of age, about fifty-two percent were female, and they represented diverse disciplines including psychology, medicine, and law.
scenes.layout_description: A profile card outlines demographic facts alongside simple symbols of medicine, psychology, and law.
scenes.visual_prompt: Sketched demographic card displaying gender percentage and age beside small ink icons of a brain, stethoscope, and scales.

scenes.narration: Before the four-hour training session began, most undergraduate students indicated having no or little prior experience concerning the use of time management strategies.
scenes.layout_description: A bar chart compares students with no or little experience against those with moderate background.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn bar chart in black ink showing a tall bar for little or no experience accented with yellow fill.

scenes.narration: Checking training transfer, trainees showed a nearly significant increase in time management behavior at two weeks and a significant increase at four weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A rising step chart marks the behavioral increase across baseline, two weeks, and four weeks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Line graph showing behavior scores rising across three points, with the four-week point circled in orange ink.

scenes.narration: In the repeated-measurement MANOVA, participating trainees reported significantly less perceived stress two weeks after training, and this significant reduction persisted at four weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A stress gauge drops from high baseline to a lower post-training score with orange indicator marks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple dial gauge drawing showing an ink needle shifting from a high stress zone down into a lower zone.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time exhibited only a tendency at two weeks, but increased significantly four weeks post-training, demonstrating a notable time lag in effects.
scenes.layout_description: An hourglass transitions into an expanding graph line highlighting the four-week mark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink sketch of an hourglass flowing into a steadily climbing line graph that turns solid yellow at four weeks.

scenes.narration: Crucially, self-reported demands showed no significant changes at two weeks or four weeks, supporting the conclusion that improvements stemmed from the training program.
scenes.layout_description: A horizontal flat line for external demands sits beneath statistical significance markers.
scenes.visual_prompt: Drawing of a steady horizontal black line representing perceived demands, enclosed in a calm yellow rectangle.

scenes.narration: Trainees with no or little prior experience showed effect sizes more than twice as strong as those entering with moderate or some experience.
scenes.layout_description: Two comparative bars highlight the difference in effect sizes between novice and experienced trainees.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two vertical bars drawn side by side, the novice bar twice as tall and filled with warm orange hatching.

scenes.narration: The authors suggest that prioritizing provides study orientation, while daily planning and monitoring reinforce completed tasks, diminishing perceived stress and enhancing personal time control.
scenes.layout_description: A roadmap sketch connects prioritizing to daily task completion and calm study focus.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn roadmap with road markers for orientation, daily planning, and task completion leading to a calm desk.

scenes.narration: Study limitations include a small final sample size, about half dropping out across follow-ups, and the lack of a randomized control comparison group.
scenes.layout_description: Three caution signposts list the primary methodological limitations noted in the paper's discussion.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three sketch caution flags in black ink with yellow exclamation marks highlighting sample size and dropout rate.

scenes.narration: The authors conclude that time management training might benefit undergraduate student well-being, though larger intervention studies are needed to establish robust empirical conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: A forward-looking path leads toward a graduation cap beside open books and a clean desk.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist ink illustration of an open path leading toward academic success, framed by soft yellow light accents.
